Who We Help  /  Non-profits

Your budget should go to the mission.

Everything we do for a small business we do for a nonprofit: the same help desk, the same planning, the same people. What changes is what sits around the technology — a board, a funder, a volunteer roster, and a budget that answers to all three.

We know what a program officer wants to see in a technology line item, and what a board needs to hear before it approves one. That context is usually the part a vendor skips.

We know how nonprofits work

Annual reporting and grant proposals

Scopes, quotes, and written assessments you can attach to an application, a funder report, or the annual report — in language a program officer will read without translating.

Technology that serves the mission

Before we recommend anything, we ask what it does for the people you serve. If a tool cannot earn its line in the budget, we will say so.

Discounts you may not know about

Tech for Good, TechSoup, and the nonprofit programs at Google and Microsoft. We work out what you qualify for and help you through the paperwork.

Volunteer-proof setups

Systems that survive turnover, with documentation a new coordinator can follow.

How we'd start

Discounted rates are standard here, not a favor.

  1. 01 We learn the program. What you do, who you serve, and how technology currently helps or gets in the way.
  2. 02 We write it down. A short assessment you can hand to a board, a funder, or your next hire.
  3. 03 We work at your pace. Around grant cycles, seasonal programs, and the weeks when everyone is at an event.

Technology help for people, and their businesses, organizations, and communities.
